prompt: Stage 5-1, four players left. You lost to Seat 4 last round because their two assassins dove your carry in the bottom-right corner. Scouting now, you see they have not touched their board, but you know Seat 4 scouts every round and reacts. You will fight Seat 4 again in two rounds; this round you fight Seat 6, whose board is a slow melee frontline with no divers. What do you do with your carry this round?

lobby.note: Assassins in both back corners; scouts and repositions every round
Six melee frontliners, no divers, no area damage
AP board, backline caster in the centre

options.label: Leave the carry in the corner this round; against Seat 6 the corner is fine and it gives Seat 4 nothing new to react to
Move the carry to the centre now so it is safe for Seat 4 in two rounds
Swap the carry to the bottom-left corner now, so Seat 4 sees the new corner and adjusts

explanation:
Positioning is a per-round decision against a specific opponent, and this round's opponent has no divers, so the corner is the best hex: maximum distance from a melee frontline. Moving now costs you nothing against Seat 6 but shows Seat 4 the change two rounds early, and a player who scouts every round will re-aim the assassins. The information you give away is worth more than the convenience of setting up early.

The play against Seat 4 happens in the planning phase of that round: leave the carry in the corner until the last three seconds, then swap it to the centre or the opposite corner after their scout is over. That is a Master-level habit, and it only works if you have not already shown your hand.
principle: Position for this round's opponent, and change position against a scouting opponent only at the last second.
commonMistake: Fixing the corner problem immediately because the last loss hurt, and letting the opponent scout the fix.
